# Story 26.1: Red-phase tests for column spread (flex-grow) in dms-base-table

**Status:** backlog
**Epic:** Epic 26 — Restore column spreading to fill row width while honoring configured widths
**Phase:** Unit Test (red phase)
**SPRIG Phase:** RED
**Estimated Duration:** 30 minutes
**Dependencies:** None (reads existing `base-table.component.scss`)

## Story

As a developer,
I want red-phase unit tests asserting that `.dms-header-cell` and `.dms-body-cell` in `dms-base-table` use a flex shorthand with grow enabled (`flex: 1 1 auto`) so columns spread to fill the row width while configured widths still render as their basis,
So that Story 26.2 has a defined, executable contract to make pass and the regression where columns stopped spreading is locked in.

## Acceptance Criteria

**Given** `apps/dms-material/src/app/shared/components/base-table/base-table.component.scss` currently declares `flex: 0 1 auto;` on both `.dms-header-cell` (line ~83) and `.dms-body-cell` (line ~148), which disables flex-grow so each cell takes only its configured width and the row no longer fills
**When** new unit tests are written that extract the top-level `.dms-header-cell { ... }` and `.dms-body-cell { ... }` rule bodies from the SCSS source and assert each declares a flex shorthand with grow = 1 and basis `auto` (i.e. matches `/flex:\s*1\s+1\s+auto/`)
**Then** every newly written test is marked `.skip()` in code (`it.skip`) so the dms-material Vitest suite runs green BEFORE Story 26.2 exists — red-phase by skip, not by failure

## Tasks

### Task 1.1: Create the column-spread spec file (red phase)

**File:** `apps/dms-material/src/app/shared/components/base-table/base-table-column-spread.spec.ts`
**Description:** Add a new vitest suite that reads `base-table.component.scss` from disk and asserts the flex rule on both cell selectors. Because this test environment does not inject component SCSS into the DOM (verified — computed styles resolve empty on a rendered cell), the tests assert the source rule text rather than `getComputedStyle`, matching the Story 8.x convention in `base-table-numeric-alignment.spec.ts`.

**Implementation Guidance:**
1. Read the SCSS with `readFileSync(path.join(__dirname, 'base-table.component.scss'), 'utf-8')` (same pattern as `base-table-numeric-alignment.spec.ts`).
2. Add a helper that locates an exact top-level selector line (e.g. `.dms-header-cell {`) at column 0 and returns the rule body up to the matching closing brace, using depth counting on `{`/`}` — reuse the approach of `numericCellRuleBody()` in `base-table-numeric-alignment.spec.ts`. Match the exact line so `.dms-body-cell--numeric {` is not mistaken for `.dms-body-cell {`.
3. Write two tests:
   - `it('should enable flex-grow on .dms-header-cell (flex: 1 1 auto)')` — assert the header rule body matches `/flex:\s*1\s+1\s+auto/`.
   - `it('should enable flex-grow on .dms-body-cell (flex: 1 1 auto)')` — assert the body rule body matches `/flex:\s*1\s+1\s+auto/`.
4. Mark both tests `.skip()` (`it.skip(...)`) so CI stays green before Story 26.2. Add a file-top comment explaining this is the TDD RED phase for Epic 26 and that Story 26.2 unskips, confirms red, then implements.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- The new spec file exists at `apps/dms-material/src/app/shared/components/base-table/base-table-column-spread.spec.ts`.
- Both tests are present and marked `.skip()`.
- No production code is modified in this story.

### Task 1.2: Verify the suite runs green with skipped tests

**File:** (verification only)
**Description:** Run the dms-material unit test suite for the new spec file to confirm it collects, both tests report as skipped, and nothing else regresses.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- `pnpm --filter dms-material test base-table-column-spread` runs green with 2 skipped tests (or the equivalent Nx/vitest invocation used by this project).
- No other spec is affected.

## Dev Notes

### Root cause (corrects the Epic prose)

The Epic description suspects Epic 20, but Epic 20 was theming-only (`--dms-*` tokens into Tailwind `theme.extend`, dead-class removal) and never touched table layout. The actual regression came from **Story 10.3** (commit `39908d7d`, "E2E test for column widths fitting content"), which added:

```scss
// .dms-header-cell and .dms-body-cell
flex: 0 1 auto;   // grow=0, shrink=1, basis=auto
```

Material MDC's default is `mat-cell, mat-header-cell { flex: 1 }` (= `1 1 0%`, basis 0), which made the inline `[style.width.px]` binding inert — every column got an equal share and configured widths were ignored. Story 10.3 fixed that by switching to `flex: 0 1 auto` (basis = configured width). The side effect is `flex-grow: 0`: cells now take exactly their configured width and never expand, so the row no longer fills — the "columns stopped spreading" symptom Epic 26 reports.

### Why `flex: 1 1 auto` is the target contract

- `basis: auto` keeps the inline `[style.width.px]` as each column's starting size (configured widths still render — Story 10.3's fix is preserved).
- `grow: 1` restores spreading: any spare row width is distributed proportionally across columns, so they fill the row again.
- `shrink: 1` is retained from Story 10.3 for narrow viewports (columns can still compress when total configured width exceeds the container).

Header and body cells share the identical rule, so header/body width parity (asserted by `base-table-two-region-regression.spec.ts`) holds under either value — this change does not break that invariant. The ex-date width e2e (`universe-ex-date-column-width.spec.ts`, asserts ≥ 200px at a 1920px viewport) only gets wider, so it stays green.

### Test vehicle rationale

The fix is pure SCSS. jsdom has no layout engine and does not inject component styles, so `getComputedStyle` cannot observe the flex value (verified in this codebase). The established convention for asserting a base-table CSS rule from a unit test is to read the SCSS source and match the rule text (`base-table-numeric-alignment.spec.ts` does exactly this for `.dms-body-cell--numeric`). This keeps the red-phase signal genuine, fast, and deterministic.
